Subject: Initial list of operational questions for air-gapped deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was really encouraged by the latency numbers. We’re actively evaluating Redwood Private for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment. Before we get to any procurement conversation, our security and infra teams need to validate a few operational constraints. I collected the initial questions and attached them (Thermexa_IT_Questions.pdf). Key items below:

- Upgrade process: In an air-gapped environment, how do you deliver patches/feature upgrades? Is there an "offline bundle" we can download and apply? What are the rollback options?
- Validation: Do you provide a staging approval bundle (so our engineers can run smoke tests) prior to production upgrade?
- Hardware compatibility: Recommended GPU/CPU configs and minimums. We have a mix of A40 and older V100 hosts; want to know what’s supported and the performance tradeoffs.
- Maintenance windows & hotfixes: How do you handle security hotfixes that are high priority? Any remote-runner or do all upgrades require physical media transfer?
- Interruption policy: Is there a graceful drain for in-flight inference and KV cache migration during upgrades?
- Offline ops: What tooling is available for log export, metrics collection, and support bundles without internet egress?
- Key management: Does Redwood integrate with customer-managed HSMs on-prem for encryption keys?

We also attached a high-level network diagram (network-drawing.png) that shows the isolation model we typically run (no outbound internet from the inference subnet).

Can you please provide a short written response we can pass to our security/compliance review? If it helps, loop in an engineer — I can set up a 45-minute technical Q&A next week.

Appreciate it,

Tasha Bennett
Head of IT Operations
Thermexa Biotech

Hi Tasha — thanks for the detailed list and the diagram. Really helpful context. I summarized the short answers below and proposed next steps so your security/compliance and infra teams have something concise for review. Marcus (cc'd) will add technical detail in a follow-up.

Short answers / summary:
- Offline upgrade bundle: Yes — we produce an "airgap bundle" (signed tarball) containing the runtime, model artifacts (if requested), and a reconciliation script. Customers can transfer the bundle via removable media or an approved internal artifact repo. The bundle includes a checksum and a signature you can validate against our public key.
- Staging approval: We provide a staging bundle and a smoke-test script that returns a pass/fail exit code for automation. Recommended flow: run staging bundle, run smoke tests, approve, then apply production bundle.
- Hardware: Certified configs include modern Ampere-class GPUs (A10/A30/A40) and newer x86 hosts. V100 is supported but you should expect lower throughput and potentially higher tail latency. Marcus: see notes for exact minimums and NVMe recommendations.
- Hotfixes & critical security patches: For critical patches we produce a micro-bundle with only the patched binaries and delta instructions to minimize transfer size. Rollback uses the last known-good bundle and a snapshot restore process we run via the offline tool.
- In-flight requests & cache: The runtime supports graceful drain and KV cache snapshotting. We recommend at least a 5–10 minute maintenance window for large KV caches during major upgrades.
- Offline telemetry/logs: Support bundle generation is fully offline; logs and metrics can be exported as encrypted archives and handed to Redwood for offline analysis.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS with integration points for HSM-backed keys. We'll need a short KMS design call to confirm your vendor and network constraints.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marcus to reply with hardware minimums, expected bundle sizes, and staging/production timing guidelines.
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical Q&A with your infra + security + our engineers (Marcus + Vivek). Proposed windows: Tue 02/24 10–11am PT or Wed 02/25 2–3pm PT.
3) We'll share the airgap upgrade doc and a sample smoke-test script ahead of the call. Link: https://redwood.ai/docs/private/offline-upgrades

I attached the briefing note I'll pass to our support team. Let me know which slot works and I'll lock it in.

Hi Tasha — Marcus from Redwood infra here. Adding the technical specifics you requested so your ops/security folks can validate. TL;DR at top, details below.

TL;DR
- Minimum recommended (small prod pool): 4x A40 (or 8x A10), 1RU NVMe per host for model cache, 256GB system RAM, 2 x 10GbE for management + data isolation.
- V100 supported for evaluation but expect ~35–50% lower throughput vs A40 for our Llama-style backbones.
- Typical offline bundle sizes: full runtime + models ~ 40–120GB depending on model family. Micro-bundles (security hotfixes) are typically <50MB–200MB.
- Staging window: 30–60 minutes for smoke tests on a staging subset; production rollout for each rack ~15–25 minutes if no model migration is required.

Details
1) Hardware & storage
- GPUs: Ampere family (A10/A30/A40) are our certified baseline. For inference-heavy workloads with >200 RPS at 512 tokens, we recommend 4+ GPUs per node. Older pascal/volta cards (V100) are still supported but require tuning; we can provide a per-model performance estimate if you share target queries/sec and average token length.
- Storage: Local NVMe for model caching is strongly recommended (1–2TB depending on model mix). Network filesystems are possible but add latency and complexity for air-gapped setups.
- CPU/RAM: 64–128 vCPU equivalent and 256GB RAM per host for multi-model serving scenarios.

2) Offline upgrade workflow
- We produce signed tarballs with a manifest.json and checksums. The offline tool provides install.sh that validates signatures and runs preflight checks (disk, docker/runtime versions).
- Smoke tests: our smoke-test script performs a small set of deterministic prompts and checks token-level outputs and latency thresholds. Exit code indicates pass/fail.
- Rollback: our installer snapshots container images and config; rollback is triggered by the offline tool with a single CLI command. We recommend taking a KV cache snapshot before production upgrades.

3) Security/hardening
- Keys: we support PKCS#11 HSMs and can integrate with your on-prem KMS for data-at-rest keys. For bundle verification we use RSA signatures.
- Network: the installer can be run from an isolated jump host. No outbound internet required; however, the signing/public key should be initially fetched via an approved channel and pinned.

4) Support & emergency patches
- For critical CVEs, we can produce a micro-bundle delivered on a USB or internal repo and provide step-by-step install instructions. If you want on-site assistance, we offer a paid field engagement.

5) Operational recommendations
- Staging-first: run a staging bundle on a subset of identical hardware. Use the included smoke tests and an internal canary routing for 1–2 hours before production.
- Maintenance windows: plan for 30–60 minutes per rack for major upgrades (includes preflight, install, validation).

If you can share the following, I’ll run a sizing recommendation and a quick perf projection:
- target P95 latency SLO (ms)
- expected concurrent sessions / qps at 256–512 token windows
- which models (open-source family or specify sizes) you plan to serve

Happy to discuss on the call Soojin suggested; Tue 02/24 10am PT works for me.
